newsitem.title: UK: Turkey oil refiners face busy maintenance schedule.
newsitem.headline: Turkey oil refiners face busy maintenance schedule.

text.p: Three of the four state-owned oil refineries in Turkey have begun a heavy season of scheduled maintenance shutdowns this year, said refinery sources.
One of three crude distillation units at the 226,000 barrels per day (bpd) Izmit refinery near Istanbul has been shut for a full re-vamp since January 10 and is not due to re-start until July 15.
Also, the two catalytic crackers at the plant are due to shut in sequence. The first from 14 February to 14 March and the second during April.

One of two crude units at the 226,000 bpd Izmir refinery on the west coast has recently come back on stream after closure from 10 December last year to January 17. The catalytic craker at the plant is due to close from May 2 to June 20 while two smaller units are also down this year.

The 100,000 bpd Kirikkale refinery, which together with Izmir has been processing Iraqi crude oil, is due to have several upgrading units closed for maintenance this spring. The reformer is due to close from April 19 to 10 May and the hydrocracker during May and June.
The small 22,000 bpd Batman refinery is due to partly close for maintenace in February and March.

Tupras, the state owned Turkisk Petroleum Refining company, runs four of the country's five refineries. The fifth 100,000 bpd unit at Mersin on the south coast is co-owned by Shell and the new joint venture between Mobil and British Petroleum.
